# Land Training 🏋️

![](real-fitness-logo.png)

For Marlins and above, swimmers are encouraged to join in with one hour a week of expert-led 'land training' (i.e. gym work).

We are very lucky that, through member contacts, Dolphins are able to undertake a targeted group training session for an hour weekly at [Real Fitness](https://www.real-collective.co.uk/) in Alnwick.

These sessions cost just £2.50 each, and have limited spaces.
You can sign up via their website. 

To book a session, select the Saturday 10:15 'Dolphins S and C Training' entry
in their diary on the landing page and follow instructions to book a slot.

## Why do we train on land?

Collette (a.k.a Colls) of Real Fitness says:

The gym lets us do things the pool simply cannot. 
We can add resistance, build strength and develop power in ways that are not possible in water, where the body is supported and the resistance changes with how fast they move. 
It also means their bones get loading they would not otherwise get, which matters during the teenage years when a large proportion of adult bone is laid down.
None of this replaces swimming. 
It complements it, and the two together tend to produce better swimmers than swimming alone.
 
Starts and turns are the moments in a race where the feet are pressed against something solid, and that is where leg strength really shows. 
In a sprint, the start can account for a good chunk of the race, and the turns even more in a short course pool. 
Strength and power measured on land line up closely with how well swimmers do both. 
The evidence generally points the same way: swimmers who train in the pool and on land tend to progress better than those who only swim.
 
There is also the question of control. 
However strong a swimmer is, that strength only reaches the water if they can hold themselves steady through the trunk, ribs, shoulders and hips. 
A good deal of what we do is building that.

A note on safety:
 
Strength training for young people is well supported when it is properly supervised and sensibly prescribed. 
It does not affect growth or growth plates, and injury rates are lower than in most field sports. 
We do want to challenge them, because that is where the benefit comes from, but I always take a view on how they arrive and adjust the session accordingly.
